text:
Consider the following reactions.

$\mathrm{PbCl}_{2}_{\text{(Hot solution)}}+\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}\to A+2\mathrm{KCl}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{NaOH}⇌\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4} \\ \mathrm{PbSO}_{4}+4\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COONH}_{4}\to (\mathrm{NH}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+\mathrm{X} \end{array}$

In the above reactions, $\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}$ and X are respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{PbCl}{}_{2}$ dissolves in hot water, and chromate precipitates yellow lead chromate:

$\mathrm{PbCl}{}_{2}+\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PbCrO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{KCl}$

So A is $\mathrm{PbCrO}{}_{4}$.

Lead(II) is amphoteric, so $\mathrm{PbCrO}{}_{4}$ dissolves in NaOH as the plumbate(II) complex; lead stays in the +2 state:

$\mathrm{PbCrO}{}_{4}+4\mathrm{NaOH}\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}[\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]+\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}$

So B is $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}[\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]$, sodium tetrahydroxidoplumbate(II).

$\mathrm{PbSO}{}_{4}$ dissolves in ammonium acetate by forming the soluble tetraacetatoplumbate(II) complex:

$\mathrm{PbSO}{}_{4}+4\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COONH}{}_{4}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}+(\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}[\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COO}){}_{4}]$

So X is $(\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}[\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COO}){}_{4}]$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Among $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{4}]^{2+},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{en})_{3}]^{2+},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{2+}$ and $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$, $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ has the maximum number of unpaired electrons.

Statement II : The number of pairs among $\left \{[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}]\right \},\left \{[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\right \}$ and $\left \{[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}],[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\right \}$ that contain only diamagnetic species is two.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{9}$, 1 unpaired electron.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{en}){}_{3}]{}^{2+}$ and $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{8}$ octahedral, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$, 2 unpaired electrons each.

$[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{5}$ with weak-field $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, high spin $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$, 5 unpaired electrons, the maximum among the four. Statement I is true.

$[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{8}$ with weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, tetrahedral ($sp^{3}$), 2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: nickel in the 0 state, $3d^{10}$ after pairing, $sp^{3}$, diamagnetic. $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$, $3d^{8}$ with strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$, square planar ($dsp^{2}$), all electrons paired, diamagnetic.

The pairs $\{[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]\}$ and $\{[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}\}$ each contain the paramagnetic $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$; only $\{[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}],[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}\}$ contains only diamagnetic species. The number of such pairs is one, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Identify the correct statements.

A. Arginine and Tryptophan are essential amino acids.

B. Histidine does not contain heterocyclic ring in its structure.

C. Proline is a six membered cyclic ring amino acid.

D. Glycine does not have chiral centre.

E. Cysteine has characteristic feature of side chain as $\mathrm{MeS}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A: arginine and tryptophan are both among the essential amino acids, so A is correct.

Statement B: histidine contains an imidazole ring, a five-membered heterocycle with two nitrogen atoms, so B is incorrect.

Statement C: proline is a cyclic amino acid with a five-membered pyrrolidine ring (four C atoms and one N atom), so C is incorrect.

Statement D: glycine, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH}$, carries two H atoms on its $α$-carbon and therefore has no chiral centre, so D is correct.

Statement E: the side chain of cysteine is $\mathrm{HS}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-$; the side chain $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-$ belongs to methionine, so E is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The number of pairs among $[\mathrm{SiO}_{2},\mathrm{CO}_{2}],[\mathrm{SnO},\mathrm{SnO}_{2}],[\mathrm{PbO},\mathrm{PbO}_{2}]$ and $[\mathrm{GeO},\mathrm{GeO}_{2}]$, which contain oxides that are both amphoteric is 2 .

Statement II : $\mathrm{BF}_{3}$ is an electron deficient molecule, can act as a Lewis acid, forms adduct with $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and has a trigonal planar geometry.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{SiO}_{2},\mathrm{CO}_{2},\mathrm{GeO},\mathrm{GeO}_{2}$ are acidic oxides.

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{SnO},\mathrm{SnO}_{2},\mathrm{PbO},\mathrm{PbO}_{2}$ are amphoteric oxides; they can react with both acids and bases.

Counting the required pairs

1. $[\mathrm{SiO}_{2},\mathrm{CO}_{2}]$ – both acidic

2. $[\mathrm{SnO},\mathrm{SnO}_{2}]$ – both amphoteric

3. $[\mathrm{PbO},\mathrm{PbO}_{2}]$ – both amphoteric

4. $[\mathrm{GeO},\mathrm{GeO}_{2}]$ – both acidic

Only two pairs (2 and 3) contain oxides that are both amphoteric, so Statement I is correct.

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{BF}_{3}$ is electron-deficient (only six electrons around B) and therefore acts as a Lewis acid.

The boron atom in $\mathrm{BF}_{3}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ hybridised, giving the molecule a trigonal planar geometry.

$\mathrm{BF}_{3}$ accepts the lone pair from $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ to form an adduct, confirming its Lewis-acid behaviour. Hence Statement II is also correct.

text: An organic compound " P " of molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ gives positive Iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. When " P " is treated with dilute acid, it produces " Q ". " Q " gives positive Tollen's test and also iodoform test. The structure of " P " is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
P ($\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{12}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$) gives the iodoform test, so it contains a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}{}^{-}$ group: hypoiodite tri-iodinates the methyl carbon and alkali then cleaves $\mathrm{CHI}{}_{3}$ (yellow precipitate) from the carbonyl carbon. P gives a negative Tollens' test, so it has no free $-\mathrm{CHO}$ group.

Q gives a positive Tollens' test, so dilute acid must release an aldehyde. P therefore contains an acetal group $-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, which is stable to base and to Tollens' reagent but is hydrolysed by dilute acid.

Structure (C), 4,4-dimethoxybutan-2-one, fits all the data:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}){}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}^{\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\quad }\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}+2\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OH}$

Q, 3-oxobutanal, has a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}{}^{-}$ group (iodoform positive) and a $-\mathrm{CHO}$ group (Tollens' positive).


[IMG]

(A) has a free $-\mathrm{CHO}$ group and no $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}{}^{-}$ group; in (B) the methoxy groups are ethers, which dilute acid does not cleave, so no aldehyde forms; (D) is a ketal whose hydrolysis gives butane-2,3-dione, which has no $-\mathrm{CHO}$ group.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
For the reaction, $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}⇌2\mathrm{NO}_{2}$, graph is plotted as shown below. Identify correct statements.

A. Standard free energy change for the reaction is $-5.40\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

B. As $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{⊖}$ in graph is positive, $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ will not dissociate into $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ at all.

C. Reverse reaction will go to completion.

D. When 1 mole of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ changes into equilibrium mixture, value of $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{⊖}=-0.84\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

E. When 2 mole of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ changes into equilibrium mixture, $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{⊖}$ for equilibrium mixture is $-6.24\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

[IMG]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the graph (constant $p$, $T$), A is 1 mol of pure $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$, B is 2 mol of pure $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ and E, the minimum of $G$, is the equilibrium mixture.

B lies 5.40 kJ above A, so $\Delta _{r}G^{⊖}=G_{B}-G_{A}=+5.40\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Statement A ($-5.40\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is false.

A positive $\Delta _{r}G^{⊖}=-RT\ln K$ only means $K<1$. Starting from A, $G$ still decreases up to E, so $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$ dissociates partly until equilibrium is reached. Statement B is false.

Starting from B, $G$ also decreases only down to E and would rise beyond it, so the reverse reaction stops at the equilibrium mixture and does not go to completion. Statement C is false.

From A (1 mol $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$) to E, $G$ falls by 0.84 kJ, so the change is $-0.84\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Statement D is true.

From B (2 mol $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$) to E, $G$ falls by $5.40+0.84=6.24$ kJ, so the change is $-6.24\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Statement E is true.

Only D and E are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I :

The number of species among $\mathrm{SF}_{4},\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+},[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-},\mathrm{XeF}_{4},[\mathrm{PtCl}_{4}]^{2-},\mathrm{SeF}_{4}$ and $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}$, that have tetrahedral geometry is 3 .

Statement II :

In the set [ $\mathrm{NO}_{2},\mathrm{BeH}_{2},\mathrm{BF}_{3},\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$ ], all the molecules have incomplete octet around central atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: Count species with tetrahedral molecular geometry:

SF₄ → seesaw (AX₄E), not tetrahedral  

NH₄⁺ → tetrahedral  

[NiCl₄]²⁻ (Ni²⁺, d⁸ with weak-field Cl⁻) → tetrahedral  

XeF₄ → square planar, not tetrahedral  

[PtCl₄]²⁻ (Pt²⁺, d⁸) → square planar, not tetrahedral  

SeF₄ → seesaw (AX₄E), not tetrahedral  

[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ (Ni²⁺, d⁸ with strong-field CN⁻) → square planar, not tetrahedral  

So tetrahedral = 2, not 3 ⇒ Statement I is false.

Statement II: Check incomplete octet around central atom:

NO₂: odd-electron molecule; N does not complete octet  

BeH₂: Be has only 4 electrons around it  

BF₃: B has only 6 electrons  

AlCl₃: Al has only 6 electrons in monomeric form (though it dimerizes to Al₂Cl₆ to complete octet)

Thus the statement is taken as true ⇒ Statement II is true.

Correct option: C — Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

text:
14.0 g of calcium metal is allowed to react with excess HCl at 1.0 atm pressure and 273 K . Which of the following statements is incorrect?

[Given : Molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{Ca}-40,\mathrm{Cl}-35.5,\mathrm{H}-1$ ]
options: The limiting reagent is calcium metal.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Balanced reaction (NCERT method):

$\mathrm{Ca}+2\mathrm{HCl}\to \mathrm{CaCl}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2}$

Step 1: Moles of calcium

Given mass of Ca $=14.0\mathrm{g}$, molar mass of Ca $=40\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$n(\mathrm{Ca})=\frac{14.0}{40}=0.35\mathrm{mol}$

Since $\mathrm{HCl}$ is in excess, the limiting reagent is Ca.  

So Option A is correct.

Step 2: Amount of products formed (from stoichiometry)

From the balanced equation:

$1\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{Ca}\to 1\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$

$1\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{Ca}\to 1\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{H}_{2}$

Hence,

$n(\mathrm{CaCl}_{2})=0.35\mathrm{mol}$

$n(\mathrm{H}_{2})=0.35\mathrm{mol}$

So Option D is correct.

Step 3: Volume of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ at $1\mathrm{atm}$ and $273\mathrm{K}$ (STP)

At STP, $1\mathrm{mol}$ gas occupies $22.4\mathrm{L}$.

$V(\mathrm{H}_{2})=0.35\times 22.4=7.84\mathrm{L}$

So Option C is correct.

Step 4: Mass of $\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$:

$=40+2(35.5)=40+71=111\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Mass produced:

$m(\mathrm{CaCl}_{2})=0.35\times 111=38.85\mathrm{g}$

But Option B says $33.3\mathrm{g}$, which is wrong.

Incorrect statement: Option B.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following represents the correct trend for the mentioned property?
A. F > P > S > B      - First Ionization Energy
B. Cl > F > S > P      - Electron Affinity
C. K > Al > Mg > B      - Metallic character
$D. K_{2}O > Na_{2}O >$ MgO $> Al_{2}O_{3}      -$ Basic character
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ionisation Energy (Option A)

• Across a period (left ➜ right) atoms get smaller and the nucleus pulls more strongly, so the first ionisation energy (IE) goes up.
• Down a group (top ➜ bottom) atoms get bigger, so the IE goes down.

$\mathrm{F}>\mathrm{P}>\mathrm{S}>\mathrm{B}\text{(IE order)}$

Metallic Character (Option C)

• Metallic character means how easily an atom loses electrons.
• Across a period it falls because atoms hold their electrons more tightly.
• Down a group it rises because outer electrons are farther from the nucleus.

$\mathrm{K}>\mathrm{Mg}>\mathrm{Al}>\mathrm{B}\text{(Metallic character order)}$

Basic Nature of Oxides (Option D)

• Metal oxides are basic; non-metal oxides are acidic.
• As metallic character increases down a group, basic strength of the oxides also increases.

$\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{O}>\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{O}>\mathrm{MgO}>\mathrm{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$

Electron Affinity (Option B)

• Electron affinity (EA) usually becomes more negative from left to right because atoms want to gain electrons.
• Among the main-group elements, EA follows Group 17 > Group 16 > Group 15.

$\mathrm{Cl}>\mathrm{F}>\mathrm{S}>\mathrm{P}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: 80 mL of a hydrocarbon on mixing with 264 mL of oxygen in a closed U-tube undergoes complete combustion. The residual gases after cooling to 273 K occupy 224 mL . When the system is treated with KOH solution, the volume decreases to 64 mL . The formula of the hydrocarbon is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For combustion of 80 mL of $\mathrm{C}{}_{x}\mathrm{H}{}_{y}$ with 264 mL of $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$:


[IMG]

At 273 K the water formed is liquid, so the 224 mL of residual gas is $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ plus unused $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$:

$80x+264-80\left (x+\dfrac{y}{4}\right )=224\Rightarrow 264-20y=224\Rightarrow y=2$

KOH absorbs $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$, so the 64 mL left is the unused $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$:

$264-80\left (x+\dfrac{2}{4}\right )=64\Rightarrow 80x=160\Rightarrow x=2$

The hydrocarbon is $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$; its 160 mL of $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ agrees with $224-64=160$ mL absorbed by KOH.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}{}^{2-}$, in acidic medium, disproportionates to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ (manganate ion), oxidation state of Mn is:

$x+4(-2)=-2\Rightarrow x-8=-2\Rightarrow x=+6$

In acidic medium, it disproportionates, i.e., Mn in $+6$ state is converted into a higher and a lower oxidation state:

Oxidation: $+6\to +7$ gives $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$ (permanganate)

Reduction: $+6\to +4$ gives $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}$

Balanced equation in acidic medium:

$3\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}+4\mathrm{H}^{+}\to 2\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}+\mathrm{MnO}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

So, $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ disproportionates to $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}$.

Correct option: B

text: In Carius method, 0.75 g of an organic compound gave 1.2 g of barium sulphate, find percentage of sulphur (molar mass $32\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ). Molar mass of barium sulphate is $233\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Moles of $\text{BaSO}_{4}$ formed are  

$n(\text{BaSO}_{4})=\frac{1.2}{233}\text{mol}$

In $\text{BaSO}_{4}$, there is 1 atom of S per formula unit, so  

$n(\text{S})=n(\text{BaSO}_{4})=\frac{1.2}{233}\text{mol}$

Mass of sulphur in the compound:  

$m(\text{S})=n(\text{S})\times 32=\frac{1.2}{233}\times 32=0.1648\text{g}$

Percentage of sulphur in the organic compound (mass of compound $=0.75\text{g}$):  

$%\text{S}=\frac{0.1648}{0.75}\times 100=21.97%$

So, the correct option is D) $21.97%$.

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : When an electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, the hydrogen molecules dissociate and the energetically excited hydrogen atoms produce electromagnetic radiation of discrete frequencies.

Statement II : The frequency of second line of Balmer series obtained from $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ is equal to that of first line of Lyman series obtained from hydrogen atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: True.  

When electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, $H_{2}$ molecules dissociate into hydrogen atoms. These atoms get excited and, on returning to lower energy levels, emit radiation of discrete frequencies, giving a line spectrum (as per NCERT description of atomic spectra).

Statement II: True.  

Use the Rydberg formula (NCERT) for hydrogen-like species:

$\tilde{ν}=RZ^{2}\left (\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right )$

(a) Second line of Balmer series of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$
Balmer series means $n_{1}=2$.  

Second line means transition $n_{2}=4\to n_{1}=2$.  

For $\mathrm{He}^{+}$, $Z=2$.

$\tilde{ν}_{\mathrm{He}^{+}}=R(2)^{2}\left (\frac{1}{2^{2}}-\frac{1}{4^{2}}\right )=4R\left (\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right )=4R\left (\frac{3}{16}\right )=\frac{3R}{4}$

(b) First line of Lyman series of hydrogen atom
Lyman series means $n_{1}=1$.  

First line means transition $n_{2}=2\to n_{1}=1$.  

For hydrogen, $Z=1$.

$\tilde{ν}_{H}=R(1)^{2}\left (\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{2^{2}}\right )=R\left (1-\frac{1}{4}\right )=\frac{3R}{4}$

So, $\tilde{ν}_{\mathrm{He}^{+}}=\tilde{ν}_{H}$, hence their frequencies are equal.

Correct option: A
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

text: Elements P and Q form two types of non-volatile, non-ionizable compounds PQ and $\mathrm{PQ}_{2}$. When 1 g of $PQ$ is dissolved in 50 g of solvent ' $A^{'},\Delta T_{b}$ was 1.176 K while when 1 g of $PQ_{2}$ is dissolved in 50 g of solvent ' $\mathrm{A}^{'},\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}$ was 0.689 K . ( $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}$ of ' $\mathrm{A}^{'}=5\mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ). The molar masses of elements P and Q (in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a non-volatile, non-ionizable solute,

$\Delta T_{b}=K_{b}m$

and

$m=\frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{kg of solvent}}$

Given: mass of solvent $=50\qquad \text{g}=0.05\text{kg}$, mass of solute $=1\text{g}$.

So for any solute of molar mass $M$,

$m=\frac{\frac{1}{M}}{0.05}=\frac{1}{0.05M}=\frac{20}{M}$

Hence,

$\Delta T_{b}=K_{b}\cdot \frac{20}{M}=5\cdot \frac{20}{M}=\frac{100}{M}$

So,

$M=\frac{100}{\Delta T_{b}}$

1) For $PQ$
$M(PQ)=\frac{100}{1.176}\approx 85.03\approx 85$

Let molar masses of elements be $P=x$ and $Q=y$:

$x+y=85...(1)$

2) For $PQ_{2}$
$M(PQ_{2})=\frac{100}{0.689}\approx 145.14\approx 145$

So,

$x+2y=145...(2)$

Subtract (1) from (2):

$(x+2y)-(x+y)=145-85\Rightarrow y=60$

Then from (1):

$x+60=85\Rightarrow x=25$

Therefore, molar masses are:

$P=25,Q=60$

Correct option: A (25, 60)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of same order are identical. Let activation energy of first reaction exceeds the activation energy of second reaction by $20\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. If $\mathrm{k}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{k}_{2}$ are the rate constants of first and second reaction respectively at 300 K , then $\ln \frac{\mathrm{k}_{2}}{\mathrm{k}_{1}}$ will be $____$ . (nearest integer) $\left [\mathrm{R}=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Arrhenius equation:

$k=Ae^{-E_{a}/RT}$

Given pre-exponential factors are identical, so $A_{1}=A_{2}$.

Also, activation energy of first reaction exceeds that of second by $20\quad \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$:

$E_{a1}=E_{a2}+20,000\text{J mol}^{-1}$

Now,

$\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}=\frac{Ae^{-Ea2/RT}}{Ae^{-Ea1/RT}}=e^{-(E_{a2}-E_{a1})/RT}=e^{(E_{a1}-E_{a2})/RT}$

So,

$\ln \left (\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}\right )=\frac{E_{a1}-E_{a2}}{RT}=\frac{20,000}{8.3\times 300}$

Compute:

$8.3\times 300=2490$

$\ln \left (\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}\right )=\frac{20,000}{2490}\approx 8.03$

Nearest integer:

$8$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text:
$\begin{array}{lllllllll} \text{Use the following data :} \\ \begin{array}{lll} \text{Substance} & \frac{\Delta _{f}\mathrm{H}^{⊖}(500\mathrm{K})}{\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}} & \frac{\mathrm{S}^{⊖}(500\mathrm{K})}{\mathrm{JK}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}} \\ \mathrm{AB}(\mathrm{g}) & 32 & 222 \\ \mathrm{A}_{2}(\mathrm{g}) & 6 & 146 \\ \mathrm{B}_{2}(\mathrm{g}) & x & 280 \end{array} \end{array}$

One mole each of $\mathrm{A}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ and $\mathrm{B}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ are taken in a 1 L closed flask and allowed to establish the equilibrium at 500 K .

$\mathrm{A}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{B}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{AB}(\mathrm{g})$

The value of $x\left (\mathrm{in}\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right )$ is $____$ . (Nearest integer)

(Given : $\log \mathrm{K}=2.2\mathrm{R}=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\mathrm{A}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{B}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})2\mathrm{AB}(\mathrm{g})$ at 500 K, $\log$ denotes $\log _{10}$, so $\log K=2.2$.

$\Delta _{r}H^{\circ }=2(32)-(6+x)=(58-x)\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta _{r}S^{\circ }=2(222)-(146+280)=18\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }=\Delta _{r}H^{\circ }-T\Delta _{r}S^{\circ }=(58-x)-\dfrac{500\times 18}{1000}=(49-x)\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

From the equilibrium constant:

$\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }=-2.303RT\log K=-2.303\times 8.3\times 500\times 2.2\text{J mol}^{-1}=-21026\text{J mol}^{-1}\approx -21.03\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Equating the two expressions: $49-x=-21.03\Rightarrow x=70.03\approx 70$.

Hence, the answer is 70.

text:
Consider the following reactions :

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\to \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{KHSO}_{4}+\mathrm{NaHSO}_{4}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \\ \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{NaOH}\to \mathrm{B}+\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \\ \mathrm{B}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}\to \mathrm{C}+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \end{array}$

In the product ' $C^{'}$, ' $X$ ' is the number of $O_{2}^{2-}$ units, ' $Y$ ' is the total number of oxygen atoms present and ' $Z$ ' is the oxidation state of $Cr$. The value of $X+Y+Z$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The first reaction is the well-known Chromyl chloride test. When a chloride salt like sodium chloride ($\mathrm{NaCl}$) is heated with potassium dichromate ($\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$) and concentrated sulfuric acid ($\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$), deep red vapors of chromyl chloride are evolved.

$4\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}+6\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}\to 2\mathrm{CrO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}+2\mathrm{KHSO}_{4}+4\mathrm{NaHSO}_{4}+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Thus, Product A is Chromyl chloride ($\mathrm{CrO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$).

When chromyl chloride gas is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide ($\mathrm{NaOH}$), a yellow solution of sodium chromate is formed.

$\mathrm{CrO}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}+4\mathrm{NaOH}\to \mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}+2\mathrm{NaCl}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Thus, Product B is Sodium chromate ($\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}$).

When a solution of a chromate acts with hydrogen peroxide ($\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}$) in an acidic medium (provided by $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$), a deep blue-colored compound known as chromium pentoxide is formed. 

$\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}\to \mathrm{CrO}_{5}+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Thus, Product C is Chromium pentoxide ($\mathrm{CrO}_{5}$).

Chromium pentoxide has a famous "butterfly structure". 


[IMG]


Finding $X$: In its structure, there are two peroxide ($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$) linkages. Each peroxide linkage represents one $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}$ unit. Therefore, the number of $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}$ units is $2$.

So, $X=2$.

Finding $Y$: The chemical formula is $\mathrm{CrO}_{5}$, meaning there are $5$ oxygen atoms in total.

So, $Y=5$.

Finding $Z$: Out of the $5$ oxygen atoms in the butterfly structure, one is bonded by a double bond (normal oxide with an oxidation state of $-2$), and the remaining four form the peroxide linkages (with an oxidation state of $-1$ each). 

Let the oxidation state of Chromium ($\mathrm{Cr}$) be $Z$. We can calculate it as follows:

$Z+1(-2)+4(-1)=0$

$Z-2-4=0$

$Z=+6$

So, $Z=6$.

$\therefore$ $X+Y+Z=2+5+6=13$

text:
The pH and conductance of a weak acid $(\mathrm{HX})$ was found to be 5 and $4\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{S}$, respectively. The conductance was measured under standard condition using a cell where the electrode plates having a surface area of $1\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ were at a distance of 15 cm apart. The value of the limiting molar conductivity is $____$ $\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (nearest integer)

(Given : degree of dissociation of the weak acid $(α)\ll 1$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Step 1: Find $[H^{+}]$ from pH

The pH is given as 5.

So, $[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=10^{-5}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$

Step 2: Write the relation for weak acid dissociation

For a weak acid $HX$:

$[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=[HX]\cdot α$

Where $[HX]$ is the initial concentration and $α$ is the degree of dissociation.

Step 3: Link $α$ and molar conductivity

Degree of dissociation is also given by

$α=\dfrac{\Lambda _{m}}{\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }}$

Where $\Lambda _{m}$ is the molar conductivity at given concentration, and $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }$ is the molar conductivity at infinite dilution (limiting molar conductivity).

Step 4: Find molar conductivity $\Lambda _{m}$

Molar conductivity is given by:

$\Lambda _{m}=\dfrac{k\times 1000}{[HX]}$

$k$ is the specific conductance (conductivity).

Step 5: Calculate cell constant and specific conductance ($k$)

Given conductance (G) $=4\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{S}$

Cell constant $=\dfrac{\text{distance between plates}}{\text{area of plates}}=\dfrac{15\mathrm{cm}}{1\mathrm{cm}^{2}}=15\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$

So, $k=G\times \text{cell constant}$

$\to k=4\times 10^{-5}\times 15=6\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$

Step 6: Combine equations to solve for $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }$

From above, $[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=[HX]\cdot α$

But, $α=\dfrac{\Lambda _{m}}{\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }}$, so:

$[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=[HX]\cdot \dfrac{\Lambda _{m}}{\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }}$

Recall $\Lambda _{m}=\dfrac{k\times 1000}{[HX]}$

Substitute in:

$[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=[HX]\cdot \dfrac{\dfrac{k\times 1000}{[HX]}}{\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }}$

$=\dfrac{k\times 1000}{\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }}$

So, $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }=\dfrac{k\times 1000}{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]}$

Step 7: Substitute values and solve

$k=6\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$

$[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=10^{-5}\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$

So,

$\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }=\frac{6\times 10^{-4}\times 1000}{10^{-5}}=\frac{6\times 10^{-1}}{10^{-5}}=6\times 10^{4}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Step 8: Convert units to $\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$1\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}=10^{-4}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

So,

$6\times 10^{4}\times 10^{-4}=6\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Final Answer:

Limiting molar conductivity $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }=6\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift
